title: 7 Best AI Music Generators for Songs, Video & APIs
summary: Compare 7 AI music generators for downloadable songs, soundtracks, editing and APIs, with current Udio export limits and commercial-use checks.
body_markdown:
You need music for a finished project, but a song, a background soundtrack and an API-generated section are different deliverables. Choosing from a demo alone can leave you with a track you can’t download or a workflow that doesn’t fit the edit. This guide separates full-song tools, creator soundtracks and developer APIs before comparing seven options.


You’ll see which routes fit vocals, video accompaniment, composition control and section-level revision. Start with where the music will be used, then check how you will obtain and edit the actual file. A good-sounding preview is only the first part of that decision.


## Quick answer


**Choose a full-song tool for vocals and lyrics, a soundtrack tool for video accompaniment, or an API for a product workflow.**


Suno supports downloadable songs; Udio currently keeps creation and sharing in-platform while downloads remain disabled. Compare the available delivery route before choosing a service.

## Which AI music generator should you choose?


- **Choose Magic Hour** when you want to type a prompt or lyrics, choose vocals or instrumental, and download a quick result without creating an account. It is especially convenient when the music is one part of a broader image-and-video workflow.
- **Choose Suno** when the primary deliverable is a complete song with vocals, lyrics, and a conventional song structure. Use a paid plan before generating music you intend to monetize; Suno says its free-plan songs are for non-commercial use.
- **Choose Udio** when you want to extend, remix, inpaint, or revise music inside Udio. Downloads of audio, video, and stems are currently disabled during its licensing transition, and Udio does not offer a public API, so it is not a practical export route for a new production workflow.
- **Choose ElevenLabs Music** when you need programmatic generation, long-form composition, audio references, or section-by-section edits. Commercial rights vary by subscription tier.
- **Choose Soundraw** when you need background music for YouTube, social video, product videos, client work, games, or broadcasts and want the license organized around creator use cases.
- **Choose AIVA** when MIDI, arrangement, and composer-style control matter more than one-click vocal songs.
- **Choose Mubert** when you need prompt-based background music for a repeatable video, stream, podcast, app, or business workflow.


## 1. Magic Hour: best for a fast no-sign-up trial


[Magic Hour's AI Music Generator](https://magichour.ai/products/ai-music-generator) creates songs or instrumental music from a text description or custom lyrics. You can choose vocals or instrumental output and generate up to three tracks per day without signing up. That makes it a low-friction way to test whether an AI soundtrack or song direction fits a video before committing to a paid workflow.


For a quick video-music test, the[public Magic Hour music tool](https://magichour.ai/products/ai-music-generator) offers three free tracks per day, with each free generation up to 30 seconds. Choose Instrumental for a background bed or supply your own lyrics for vocals, then listen to the complete downloaded track in the edit. A music-generation allowance is separate from the credits and controls for creating the accompanying video.


Magic Hour is the most practical choice here when music is one step in a larger media project. The same platform also includes video and image creation tools, while the separate[AI Music Video Generator](https://magichour.ai/products/ai-music-video-generator) helps turn audio into a visual piece. For the next step from a finished track to visuals, compare the[best AI music video generators](https://magichour.ai/blog/best-ai-music-video-generators) by beat sync, lyrics, references, editing, and full-song workflow.


**Best for:** creators who want to move from an idea to a downloadable track quickly.


**Watch for:** the public API documentation we checked does not list music generation. Use the browser product when you need this specific capability, and review the current output terms before commercial release.


## 2. Suno: best for complete songs with vocals


[Suno](https://suno.com/) is built around generating full songs rather than only background beds. Its current plans support song descriptions, vocals, instrumentals, audio uploads, editing, and stem separation at different tiers. That makes it a strong fit for users who want a recognizable verse-and-chorus result instead of a loop under a video.


The rights distinction matters. Suno's current help center says it owns songs generated on the free Basic plan and permits non-commercial use. It says subscribers own songs generated while on Pro or Premier and may monetize them, while separately warning that copyright protection depends on human contribution and jurisdiction.


**Best for:** full songs, vocal demos, and rapid genre exploration.


**Watch for:** do not generate on the free plan and assume a later subscription retroactively grants commercial rights. Check Suno's current terms before distribution.


## 3. Udio: in-platform editing during its licensing transition


[Udio](https://www.udio.com/) still supports song creation with its v1, v1.5, and Allegro models plus tools to extend, remix, inpaint, edit, and work from audio you own. During its current licensing transition, creations stay inside Udio and can be shared through Udio URLs, but audio, video, and stem downloads are disabled.


Udio still provides daily and monthly credits, although allowances and subscriber limits can vary by account during the transition. Its help center states that downloads are disabled and that it does not offer a public API.


**Best for:** people who want to build, revise, and share a song inside Udio during the transition.


**Watch for:** downloads of audio, video, and stems are disabled, so do not choose Udio when the deliverable is an export for YouTube, ads, a client, or distribution. Verify the current transition terms before committing work.


## 4. ElevenLabs Music: best for APIs and section-level control


[ElevenLabs Music](https://elevenlabs.io/music) v2.5 supports prompted music, audio references, long-form composition, inpainting, multilingual vocals, and mid-track changes. Its public API exposes generation and editing through the music_v2_5 model, which makes it the clearest choice in this list for developers and production systems.


**API default and website default are different.** The[Compose music endpoint](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/music/compose) currently defaults to music_v1 even though the consumer product promotes v2.5. Set model_id to music_v2_5 explicitly when that is the intended model. Choose either a prompt or a composition_plan; the endpoint does not accept both together.


**Check the plan’s permitted media and business eligibility.** The[ElevenLabs Music Terms updated October 9, 2026](https://elevenlabs.io/music-terms) list paid API access and music-streaming distribution from Creator upward. Free through Pro are individual-use plans; Scale and Business have employee-count eligibility limits. Film, television, radio and studio games require the applicable Enterprise Music rights. The table lists no Free downloads, although an older launch announcement advertises free exports: confirm the current surface and terms before budgeting a deliverable. Model resale and music-library distribution need written authorization; ordinary API access does not grant either.


**Best for:** developers, agencies, and teams that need repeatable generation or targeted edits.


**Watch for:** API access does not remove the need to record model, plan, source-audio rights, and the terms in effect for each production job.


## 5. Soundraw: best for creator-video licensing workflows


[Soundraw](https://soundraw.io/) focuses on music for videos and other creator projects. Its licensing page lists uses including YouTube, social content, product videos, tutorials, client work, games, radio, and television, with different rules for artists distributing songs built from its beats.


That use-case detail is useful when the problem is not “make me a pop single,” but “give this edit a track I can publish in the intended channel.” You still need the correct plan and must follow its rules for modifying and distributing music.


**Best for:** video creators who want music controls and a license explained by publishing use case.


**Watch for:** a creator-video license and an artist-distribution license are different. Match the plan to the actual release.


**Video soundtrack, artist release and API integration are separate purchases.**[SOUNDRAW’s license](https://soundraw.io/license) permits eligible background use, but an Artist-plan streaming release requires a beat modified so the finished song sounds different. Content ID registration is prohibited. For music inside an app or creative platform, use the[SOUNDRAW API plans](https://soundraw.io/api) and their linked API license rather than assuming the creator subscription covers an end-user generation service.


## 6. AIVA: best for MIDI and composition control


[AIVA](https://www.aiva.ai/) is aimed at composition and arrangement. Its pricing page advertises more than 250 styles, audio or MIDI influence, track editing, and multiple download formats. The free tier is for non-commercial use with attribution; AIVA's Pro tier states that the subscriber owns the full copyright to compositions created under that plan.


This makes AIVA a better fit for composers and editors who want material they can continue shaping in a digital audio workstation than for someone who only wants an instant vocal single.


**Best for:** instrumental composition, MIDI-oriented workflows, and editable scores.


**Watch for:** ownership and allowed use depend on the plan under which the track was created.


[AIVA’s Standard plan](https://www.aiva.ai/pricing) limits monetization to YouTube, Twitch, TikTok and Instagram. That differs from the Pro plan’s stated full monetization rights: do not treat a paid Standard subscription as blanket permission for every client, advertising or distribution channel.


## 7. Mubert: best for background music at scale


[Mubert](https://mubert.com/) generates background music by prompt, mood, genre, and duration. Its plan structure separates non-commercial use from creator, professional, and business uses, and it offers an API for apps and automated experiences.


Mubert is most relevant when music supports another product: a video, stream, podcast, app, or in-store experience. It is less directly aimed at the lyric-first, artist-style song workflow served by Suno and Udio.


**Best for:** repeatable background music for content and software.


**Watch for:** paid advertising, client work, apps, and business locations can require different rights. Choose the plan for the distribution channel, not only the number of tracks.


**Commercial soundtrack, not a standalone release.**[Mubert’s current plan guidance](https://mubert.com/render/pricing) labels Creator non-commercial; Pro adds monetization, while Business covers client work, agencies, apps and games. Its disclaimer prohibits standalone music redistribution, streaming-service publication and Content ID registration. After cancellation, previously published eligible projects may remain online, but old tracks cannot be used in new projects. Save the license certificate with each published project.

## How to compare AI music generators fairly


Use one brief across every compatible tool. A useful test has enough constraints to expose differences without prescribing every note:


Create a 45-second optimistic electronic soundtrack for a product launch video. Start sparse for five seconds under narration, build with warm synths and light percussion, add a clear lift at 20 seconds, and end cleanly without fading. Instrumental, 110 BPM, no recognizable melody from an existing song.


[Try in AI Music Generator](https://magichour.ai/create/ai-music-generator?prompt=Create%2520a%252045-second%2520optimistic%2520electronic%2520soundtrack%2520for%2520a%2520product%2520launch%2520video.%2520Start%2520sparse%2520for%2520five%2520seconds%2520under%2520narration%252C%2520build%2520with%2520warm%2520synths%2520and%2520light%2520percussion%252C%2520add%2520a%2520clear%2520lift%2520at%252020%2520seconds%252C%2520and%2520end%2520cleanly%2520without%2520fading.%2520Instrumental%252C%2520110%2520BPM%252C%2520no%2520recognizable%2520melody%2520from%2520an%2520existing%2520song.)


Score each result on the same five questions:


1. Does the track follow the requested structure and duration?
2. Can speech remain clear over the arrangement?
3. Does the ending cut cleanly for the edit?
4. Can you revise one weak section without restarting?
5. Does the applicable plan permit the intended channel, client, ad, or product use?


Record every attempt, not only the winner. The useful cost is **total spend divided by accepted tracks** , because a cheap generation that needs ten retries can cost more than an expensive first-pass result.


## AI song generator versus AI soundtrack generator


An AI song generator usually creates vocals, lyrics, verses, choruses, and a finished-song structure. Suno is the clearest downloadable full-song option in this guide; Udio remains an in-platform creation environment while downloads are disabled. An AI soundtrack generator prioritizes mood, timing, duration, and music that sits under dialogue or visuals. Soundraw and Mubert are closer to that workflow. ElevenLabs spans both and adds an API; Magic Hour offers fast song or instrumental creation within a broader creative suite; AIVA emphasizes composition and arrangement.


Choose based on the final deliverable. A catchy vocal song can compete with narration, while a controlled instrumental bed may be exactly what a product video needs. For advertising-specific licensing and editing questions, use our focused guide to[AI music for video ads](https://magichour.ai/blog/best-ai-music-generators-for-video-ads) . For models that generate video and sound together, see[AI video generators with native audio](https://magichour.ai/blog/best-ai-video-generators-with-native-audio) .


## Commercial use and copyright: the short answer


Paying for an AI music plan does not automatically answer every rights question. Check four separate things:


- **Contractual permission:** does the provider's plan allow monetization, paid ads, client work, distribution, or product use?
- **Input rights:** do you own the lyrics, recordings, voice, melody, or other material you uploaded?
- **Copyright eligibility:** does your jurisdiction recognize enough human authorship in the finished work?
- **Platform policy:** will your distributor, marketplace, or ad platform accept the track and its provenance?


Keep the prompt, source files, generation date, plan receipt, exported track, and a copy of the applicable terms. If the release carries material legal or financial risk, have qualified counsel review it.

Udio offers in-platform credits but currently disables downloads. “Free to generate,” “free to export,” and “free to monetize” are different claims.
